resolved_findings.title: Identify the L2 quotient used by Schwarz
resolved_findings.finding: The proof calls E(UV) an inner product on square-integrable random variables without identifying variables equal almost surely. On literal measurable functions this is only semidefinite; the linked Schwarz theorem requires an inner product space.
resolved_findings.correction: Link 0A6A/00Q6 and state the almost-sure quotient, or prove the required inequality directly from E(X-t 1_A)^2 >= 0. The displayed Paley-Zygmund inequality itself is correct.
resolved_findings.verification: The proof now explicitly uses almost-sure equivalence classes in L2 and links 0A6A; 00Q6 and the real-inner-product convention were also checked.

resolved_findings.correction: State that partial v is the set of adjacent constraints and partial a the set of adjacent variables. Recall finite-tree context in 4M0D or explicitly inherit the newly defined notation.
resolved_findings.verification: 4M0C now defines both neighbor sets; 4M0D locally binds V,F,E and inherits that notation explicitly. Branch sum and normalization cancellation remain valid.

resolved_findings.title: Require a positive second-moment comparison constant

resolved_findings.verification: 4M0S now requires 0<C<infinity, eliminating the empty-event 0/0 case. Bounded X and the rational-parameter quadratic argument are retained.

resolved_findings.verification: Optional unexplained research-method names were removed from 4M09, 4M0N and 4M0O. The cited theorem scope and positive-probability distinction remain explicit.

resolved_findings.title: Supply the product-L2 approximation step for general progressive integrands
resolved_findings.finding: The Ito isometry and extension on the closure of simple past-measurable processes are valid. The last paragraph then asserts that every progressive square-integrable process is in that closure, relying on density of finite sums 1_(a,b](t)Y(omega) in product L2 and convergence of left-step approximations. Neither this density result nor the required convergence theorem is proved or accurately linked. 0A67 is completeness, not density; 00QB only constructs product measure. Thus the declared local construction/proof still hides an essential approximation input.
resolved_findings.correction: Keep the valid simple-process argument. Supply or link a precise product-space rectangle-density/time-translation lemma and justify the final bounded left-step limit, using actual measure-theoretic prerequisites such as 0F62, 0A87, 0H53 and 0I8I as applicable. Alternatively state the general progressive-integrand extension as a precisely sourced theorem and narrow packet proof_scope. Merely linking general simple-function density does not by itself establish density of time-rectangle tensor functions.

evidence.detail: Actually read: arbitrary measurable simple functions are Lp-dense. An additional rectangle approximation argument is needed for the specific tensor class.
Actually read: Riesz-Fischer completeness; no product-rectangle density theorem.
Actually read: product sigma-algebra and measure construction, not the approximation result.
Actually read: dominated convergence, available to justify bounded pathwise step convergence.

resolved_findings.acceptance_condition: Revised 4M13 and packet accurately supply or cite the missing approximation contract; actual new prerequisite destinations must be read and hashes refreshed.
resolved_findings.verification: 4M19 proves finite-interval rectangle density by a concrete generating algebra, finite positive/negative measures, 0A87 uniqueness and 00MS orthogonal decomposition; 0I8I handles time truncation. 4M1D proves translation continuity from the explicit rectangle symmetric-difference estimate and density, then time-average convergence by Fubini-Tonelli and Schwarz. 4M13 truncates progressive integrands, preserves adaptation under past averaging, proves the pathwise 2K/h Lipschitz bound, and obtains the explicit left-step error 2K delta/h. Choosing K, h, delta in order closes the simple-process density step. The original isometry and fixed-time L2 extension remain valid. Actual prerequisite contracts were read, not inferred from titles.
